newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Eletrobras sees level 3 ADR by 1998's end.
newsitem.headline: Eletrobras sees level 3 ADR by 1998's end.

text.p: Brazilian federally owned power firm Eletrobras plans to launch a level three American Depositary Receipt (ADR) by the end of 1998, a company official said.
Eletrobras President Firmino Sampaio said the company was still adapting its balance sheet to U.S. corporate accounting standards in order to issue ADRs.
Eletrobras shares currently trade as level one ADRs on over-the-counter markets in the United States.
A level three program would allow the firm to issue new stock and list the shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Sampaio would not say how much the company planned to raise or how many shares the company would issue under a level three ADR program.
An ADR program increases the liquidity of a company's stock and gives the firm a higher profile as well as greater exposure abroad.
Sampaio also said Eletrobras posted a net profit of 2.39 billion reais in 1996 compared with 750 million reais the previous year.
